question: Does the shallow-soil wetness association with rainfall-associated strong chorus activation transport across disjoint routes, time periods and omission of individual states?
sample: Exactly the weather-qualified pairs constructed by run_naamp_soil_moisture_cue.py.
endpoint: strong_new_score (dry CI=0 to wet CI=2/3 score).
model: strong_new_score ~ rain_contrast + rain72_amount_difference_z + soil1_gain_difference_z + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber), route-clustered covariance.

route_split.pass: soil1_gain_difference_z beta >0 with complete 95% CI >0 in both folds.

temporal_split.pass: soil1_gain_difference_z beta >0 with complete 95% CI >0 in both periods.

leave_one_state_out.pass: All 21 omitted-state refits retain soil1 beta >0.
leave_one_state_out.strong_pass: All 21 omitted-state refits retain complete 95% CI >0.

state_specific: Descriptive only for states with >=100 pairs and >=15 routes; report sign and CI support.
same_observer_physical_stop: Repeat deterministic route A/B split in the existing same-observer + physically stable subset if each fold >=1000 pairs and >=200 routes.
interpretation: A pass establishes robustness within the sampled NAAMP domain, not continental or universal generality.
ERA5 swvl1 is route-scale soil-water context, not frog hydration or pond depth.
No causal mediation claim is authorized.
No RC11 manuscript modification is authorized.
